## [2026-09-30](../../../reports/2026/09/2026-09-30.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37626>)

SPLASH changes attention parallelism while requests are running by reusing resident weights and KV caches, transferring missing state in the background, and switching at a batch boundary. This lets serving systems adapt to changing concurrency and context lengths; its additional ownership layout stores attention weights and each request's cache without replicating either.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T10:02:58Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Serving, Dynamic Parallelism, KV Cache

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37626>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ict-agent/SPLASH-sglang>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. arXiv v1 was submitted 2026-09-29 at 14:02:29 UTC, inside the daily window. The SGLang-based implementation compares four layouts on B200, H200, and DCU; the authors report 1.3–1.73x throughput versus fixed layouts on B200/GLM-5.3 and measure all twelve switch directions.

**Limitations:** Main experiments use fixed output lengths and controlled concurrency sweeps. Switching needs memory headroom and pre-captured graphs; transfers contend for bandwidth, and short-lived workload changes may not repay the cost. Speculative decoding and heterogeneous workers are outside the implementation scope.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180>)

PagedAttention stores key-value caches in dynamically allocated blocks, allowing vLLM to avoid large contiguous reservations and share cached state across related sequences. More efficient memory use permits larger concurrent batches, making this a foundational open reference for high-throughput language-model serving.

**Published:** 2023-09-12 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Serving, PagedAttention, Memory Management

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180>) · [Code](<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper details cache management, scheduling, preemption, and distributed execution, with OPT and LLaMA experiments on A100 GPUs using ShareGPT- and Alpaca-derived workloads plus block-size ablations.

**Limitations:** The original comparisons use historical FasterTransformer and reimplemented Orca baselines with synthetic arrival times. Block size trades memory fragmentation against kernel efficiency; the paper does not rank current serving releases.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104>)

SGLang combines a programming interface for multi-call language-model workflows with a runtime that reuses prompt prefixes through RadixAttention and accelerates constrained decoding. This reduces repeated prefill work and exposes parallelism in agent, retrieval, and structured-output applications, making it a useful open serving reference.

**Published:** 2023-12-12 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Serving, Prefix Caching, Structured Outputs

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104>) · [Code](<https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The revised paper studies 7B–70B language models and multimodal workloads on A10G/A100 hardware, with component ablations and cache-hit measurements that explain the observed improvements.

**Limitations:** The historical comparison uses vLLM 0.2.5 and other older baselines; its headline speedup is not a ranking of current engines. Long-output workloads with little shared context show much smaller gains.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670>)

DistServe runs prompt prefill and token decoding on separate GPUs and independently chooses their resource allocations and parallelism. It increases the number of requests served within both first-token and per-token latency targets, establishing a practical foundation for disaggregated inference.

**Published:** 2024-01-18 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Prefill Decode Disaggregation, Serving, Latency SLO

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670>) · [Code](<https://github.com/LLMServe/DistServe>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The OSDI work evaluates OPT-13B/66B/175B across chat, code, and summarization workloads on 32 A100 GPUs, with bandwidth-aware placement and ablations of the disaggregation design.

**Limitations:** Results use historical engines, synthetic arrival times, and workload-specific latency targets. KV transfers need sufficient bandwidth, and the prototype leaves advanced preemption and fault tolerance to future work.
